tasks.question: Do you think students should study subjects they enjoy? Why?

models: The main reason for this is that students engage more when interested, which means that they retain information better, and so their grades improve.

cues.cue: practical subjects / prepare / students for work
models: This is because practical subjects prepare students for work, which explains why they stay motivated, and therefore they perform better.
This can be explained by the fact that forced subjects cause boredom, which accounts for the drop in effort many students show.
One explanation is that enjoyment builds confidence, and this is supported by studies on motivation, since confident students take more risks.
This is largely due to the fact that interest sustains long-term effort, and as a result students persist through difficulty, which is why they succeed.
The reason why this happens is that curiosity drives independent study, and this leads to deeper understanding, because students explore beyond the syllabus.

tasks.question: Should young people be encouraged to travel? Give your reasons.

models: This means that travel broadens the mind, and as a consequence young people become more open-minded, which is significant because it shapes their worldview.
This is because travelling exposes young people to different cultures, which explains why they develop greater empathy, and therefore they become more tolerant.
This occurs as a result of new experiences building independence, which means young people learn to solve problems alone, and over time they grow more confident.
This can be explained by the fact that travel improves language skills, which accounts for the confidence many young travellers gain in communication.
One explanation is that travel challenges assumptions, and this is supported by the way travellers often return with new perspectives, since exposure changes attitudes.
This is largely due to the fact that young travellers gain real-world skills, and as a result they adapt more easily to new situations, which is why employers value the experience.

tasks.question: Do you think everyone should learn a second language? Why?

cues.cue: a second language / open / career opportunities
models: The main reason for this is that a second language opens career opportunities, which means that speakers can work internationally, and so their prospects widen.
This is because bilingualism improves cognitive flexibility, which explains why bilingual people often solve problems more creatively, and therefore they adapt faster to new situations.
This can be explained by the fact that language learning strengthens cultural understanding, which accounts for the empathy bilingual speakers often show.

cues.cue: speaking another language / boost / travel confidence
models: One explanation is that speaking another language boosts travel confidence, and this is supported by how much easier it becomes to connect with locals, since communication removes barriers.

cues.cue: early language exposure / shape / the brain
models: The reason why this happens is that early language exposure shapes the developing brain, and this leads to stronger memory skills, because the brain builds new neural connections.
This occurs as a result of multilingual skills increasing global mobility, which means speakers can live and work almost anywhere, and over time this broadens their opportunities.

tasks.question: Should schools teach more practical life skills? Why?

models: This is because schools often neglect everyday skills, which explains why many young adults struggle with basic tasks, and therefore they feel unprepared for independence.

cues.cue: practical skills / prepare / students for adulthood
models: The main reason for this is that practical skills prepare students for adulthood, which means that graduates cope better with real responsibilities, and so they adjust more easily.
This can be explained by the fact that life-skills classes reduce financial mistakes, which accounts for the confidence young adults show when managing money.

cues.cue: learning to cook / support / healthier habits
models: One explanation is that learning to cook supports healthier habits, and this is supported by the way practical knowledge changes daily choices, since students apply what they learn.
This is largely due to the fact that practical training builds self-reliance, and as a result students feel more capable of handling challenges, which is why confidence grows.

cues.cue: life skills / bridge / theory and practice
models: In other words, life skills bridge theory and practice, and what this means is that students leave school genuinely ready for life, so the transition to adulthood is smoother.

tasks.question: Do you think cities are better places to live than the countryside? Give reasons.

models: This is because cities offer more jobs, which explains why so many people relocate there, and therefore urban populations continue to grow.
The main reason for this is that urban areas provide better services, which means that residents have easier access to healthcare and education, and so quality of life improves.
This occurs as a result of cities concentrating opportunities, which means ambitious people are drawn toward them, and over time this reshapes the population balance.

cues.cue: city life / expose / people to diversity
models: This can be explained by the fact that city life exposes people to diversity, which accounts for the broader perspectives many urban residents develop.
This is largely due to the fact that the countryside often lacks entertainment options, and as a result young people are drawn to cities, which is why rural populations shrink.
To put it differently, cities connect people to wider networks, which is to say that opportunities multiply through contact, and this drives further growth.

tasks.question: Should people spend less time on their phones? Why?

models: This can be explained by the fact that texting is cheaper than calling, which accounts for the shift toward phone-based communication.

cues.cue: excessive phone use / harm / sleep quality
models: This is because excessive phone use harms sleep quality, which explains why many people report feeling tired, and therefore reducing screen time is advised.
The main reason for this is that constant notifications disrupt concentration, which means that productivity falls, and so many people struggle to focus.

cues.cue: heavy phone use / increase / anxiety levels
models: This is largely due to the fact that heavy phone use increases anxiety levels, and as a result many users feel constantly on edge, which is why doctors recommend limits.
This occurs as a result of screen time reducing face-to-face interaction, which means relationships can weaken, and over time people may feel more isolated.

cues.cue: phone addiction / mirror / other behavioural addictions
models: One explanation is that phone addiction mirrors other behavioural addictions, and this is supported by similar patterns in brain activity, since the reward systems overlap.
